narrative.summary: Cameroon has no AI-specific law and no officially published AI strategy text. Its only binding AI-relevant instrument is Law 2024/017 on personal data protection, which requires impact assessments for high-risk processing and gives a right to object to decisions based solely on automated processing, including profiling; its 18-month compliance period ended in June 2026, but no decree setting up the data protection authority has been published. A national AI strategy led by the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications was presented in July 2025 but has not been officially published, and the Government signed the World AI Cooperation Organization constitutive act in July 2026.
narrative.review_notes: Reviewed on 12 and 13 October 2026 and re-checked on 18 October 2026, when the justice, defence, labour, territorial administration and basic education ministries' websites were reached at their current addresses and showed no AI-governance documents. The secondary education ministry's former address no longer hosts the ministry and the cyber agency's site search does not work; the national AI strategy, the data protection law's implementing decrees and the WAICO constitutive act remain leads.

instruments.official_title: Loi n°2024/017 du 23 décembre 2024 relative à la protection des données à caractère personnel au Cameroun
instruments.english_title: Law No. 2024/017 of 23 December 2024 on the protection of personal data in Cameroon
instruments.issuing_authority: Parliament of Cameroon (adopted); promulgated by the President of the Republic
instruments.current_status: Promulgated 23 December 2024 and published under the urgency procedure (art. 75; to be inserted in the Journal officiel in French and English). Article 73 gave controllers and processors 18 months from promulgation (to 23 June 2026) to comply. Art. 74 refers implementation details to further texts; no implementing decree on the Personal Data Protection Authority or on impact assessments was found in the prc.cm law and decree listings (checked to Decree 2026/334 of 16 October 2026) on 2026-10-18.
instruments.summary: Cameroon's first general personal data protection law, applying to processing by the State, decentralised local authorities and any natural or legal person in or established in Cameroon. It sets processing principles and security duties, requires a prior data protection impact assessment for any processing likely to create a high risk to individuals' rights (art. 33), and gives data subjects rights including erasure, objection, rectification, portability and the right to object to any decision based solely on automated processing of their data, including profiling (art. 44). It establishes a Personal Data Protection Authority with certification and supervisory powers and criminal penalties, including fines of up to XAF 1 billion for legal persons (art. 71).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Governs the personal data used to train and run AI systems and sets the automated-decision and profiling safeguard (art. 44) and high-risk impact assessments (art. 33).

leads.title: Stratégie Nationale de l'Intelligence Artificielle (SNIA) du Cameroun
leads.english_title: National Artificial Intelligence Strategy of Cameroon
leads.issuing_authority: Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications (MINPOSTEL), under the Prime Minister's high patronage
leads.note: Presented by the Minister of Posts and Telecommunications at the second national AI consultations (CONIA), Yaoundé, 7-8 July 2025 (press reports: vision of Cameroon as Africa's AI hub by 2040, seven pillars including an AI authority, a presidential AI council and an AI framework law). No official full text was found on minpostel.gov.cm (site search for 'intelligence artificielle', 'stratégie nationale', 'SNIA', 'CONIA'), spm.gov.cm, antic.cm or prc.cm on 2026-10-12. Record as national_strategy once an official copy or adoption act is published. 2026-10-18: minpostel.gov.cm site search for 'intelligence artificielle' (18 results) shows only news items (China AI cooperation Aug 2026, innovation week June-July 2026); still no official strategy text.
